correctness_confidence.basis: I rechecked by hand the three-vertex decomposition of Theorem 4 (vertex coefficients, weights, determinant u, Lemma 3 entropy g(u)), the Lemma 5 parameter identification (alpha delta - beta eta = k p(1-p) >= lambda^2 p(1-p)), the Theorem 1 converse/achievability logic, and the arithmetic of Proposition 12 (reversed parameters 1/4, 1/8, 5/8, 5/48 sum correctly; 1259712 > 823543). I found no error. However the whole result rests on Lemma 2, an external 2026 inequality that I could not verify; that caps my confidence.

rigor.basis: Proofs are explicit, boundary cases are treated (zero row mass, u=0, p=0,1, t=0,1), external theorems are stated precisely with their sources, and numerical results are labeled as floating-point illustrations. Some steps are terse (convex-roof concavity/continuity in Section 6, Carathéodory-type extremal-measure arguments in Prop. 8 and eq. (10)) and are asserted rather than fully worked.

novelty.basis: The extension from the amplitude-damping/pure-output boundary (lambda^2=k) to the full Davies region, strong convex-roof superadditivity, complement capacity additivity, reverse-channel closure inside the Davies family and the nonunital strict Choi-cost separation appear to be new relative to the cited work; the paper is honest that the key inequality is not its own. My web searches (two queries) located arXiv 2609.28592 but gave no evidence of a prior full-Davies additivity proof; I could not read the OpenAI note or the full text of 2609.28592, so priority is unchecked.

significance.basis: If correct, additivity of Holevo information and a single-letter classical capacity for all qubit Davies channels (including the complementary channel) would settle a long-standing class (generalized amplitude damping) and give a nontrivial simulation-cost result. The value is largely derivative of the Tang et al./OpenAI inequality, and the result is confined to one-qubit memoryless channels, so it is strong but not field-shaping.

reproducibility.basis: Formulas are explicit and examples have exact parameters, but the scripts and supplement were not available to me, I ran no code, and the numerical tables (e.g., capacity 0.5039 bits, 4-signal optimizers) are unverified by me. The author states no interval certification was done.

summary: The manuscript extends a recent triangular block-entropy inequality (Tang et al. 2026; OpenAI 2026) from amplitude damping and generalized amplitude damping on the boundary lambda^2=k to the whole qubit Davies region 0<=lambda^2<=k, via a third vertex obtained from strong subadditivity, and derives: a population-resolved output-entropy bound, strong convex-roof superadditivity, additivity of Holevo information and classical capacity C=chi for the channel and its complement with any partner, an explicit scalar convex-envelope formula, formation entropy in the Stinespring range, and parallel simulation cost of the complementary channel via a reverse-channel closure, plus a nonunital example where simulation cost strictly exceeds Choi-state cost. My hand check of the main derivations (Thm 4, Lemma 5, Thm 1, Prop 12 arithmetic) found them consistent. The central dependence on Lemma 2, a 2026 result I could not verify, and uncertified numerics are the principal reasons for a major-revision rating; no internal error was found. I did not execute code or read supplementary files.
strengths: Clear, honest delineation of antecedents (Tang et al., OpenAI, Hellmund-Uhlmann, Wilde, Amosov) and of what is not claimed (original channel simulation cost, quantum capacity, adaptive tasks).
Third-vertex argument in Thm 4 is short and checks out, including the sharpness remark (X=Y gives equality).
Reverse-channel closure inside the Davies family (k_p, lambda_p^2 <= k_p) is a neat, verifiable structural step enabling the simulation result.
Exact rational counterexample in Prop 12 with checkable arithmetic; careful limitation statements.
weaknesses: All main theorems depend on Lemma 2, an external 2026 inequality not proved here; one of the sources is a non-peer-reviewed repository note.

Several steps are sketched (continuity and concavity of G_M, extremal measures with at most two/three atoms, Kraus infimum arguments, passage from Choi-state cost to reverse-channel Stinespring range).

Numerical evidence (tables, 16000 block tests, 'Astra' audits) is floating-point only, not certified, and not independent; the AI-assisted process and prior AI review are disclosed but unreviewed by humans.
Scope limited to lambda^2 <= k (not the full phase-covariant CP region lambda^2 <= k+ab), and to the complementary channel for simulation cost; original channel simulation cost remains open.
Section 8 Lipschitz constant and hull-optimizer claims use m>0 and exclude boundary cases.
potential_errors: Prop. 12: equality G_N(p)=J(p) near p=1/2 requires the concavity condition (negative quadratic coefficient of the reversed determinant) to hold at the relevant interior reversed-population argument for p in an open interval; the manuscript states this briefly and I only checked it at p=1/2 (5/48 - 25/64 = -55/192).
Section 6: existence of a diagonal maximizer of G_{Phi^c} by phase-averaging and concavity of G_M relies on an inf-over-Kraus argument whose handling of singular inputs is only outlined.
Eq. (10)/Prop. 8: finite-support extremality (at most two or three populations) is argued by perturbation without explicit treatment of endpoint atoms and the moment constraint together.

Theorem 6 for Phi^c uses S(N^c(psi_j)) = S(N(psi_j)) for pure conditional branches; valid, but the identification of the Stinespring dilation used in Section 5 with the one in Lemma 5 is not spelled out.
strong_novelty_candidates: Additivity of Holevo information and classical capacity (chi = C, any finite-dimensional partner) for all qubit Davies channels with extra dephasing (lambda^2 <= k), including the complementary channel.
Nonunital qubit complementary channel whose parallel simulation cost strictly exceeds the cost of its Choi state (Prop. 12), via reverse-channel closure in the Davies family.
Three-vertex extension (Thm 4) of the triangular block-entropy inequality to the thermal interior.
unresolved_material_objections: The principal results rest on Lemma 2 (Tang et al. 2026, Thm 4.2; OpenAI 2026, Thm 2.1), an external inequality not proved in the manuscript and which I could not independently verify; if it fails in the stated generality (same finite rectangular shape, zero-weight conventions), Theorems 1, 4, 6, 9 and 10 fail.
